applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a row and writes the grounds for it, which is exactly the act K-S2 governs.
quote: D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings, with nothing else settling it, is such a verse.
room: Interpreted the phrase 'with nothing else settling it.' Reading 1: the citation of [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4 is the judge weighing the defender's chain, so the verdict rests on support and not on one verse. Reading 2: that citation is only a locator, and the sole substantive reason written is the verse's own two halves -- Mary's 'thy father' against the child's 'my Father's business' -- so a single verse admitting both readings is the ground of the UNDERDETERMINED verdict. I chose Reading 2 because the judge wrote no weighing of the chain and the verdict itself declares the row unsettled.
why: The judge grounds an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on the single passage Luke 2:48-49 reading both ways at once -- Mary's 'thy father' one way, the child's 'my Father's business' the other -- with nothing else written as settling it, which is the very both-readings verse K-S2 forbids as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED.
